anu-p01.speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person)
anu-p01.question: What is the method, if no method is enjoined?
premises: Six techniques denied: contemplation, speech-connection, discussion, visualization, steadying, japa-practice-effort.
The question replaces the hunt: what stands well-decided? Speak it, hear it.
The answer is two refusals and one command: not renouncer, not possessor — enjoy happiness, wholly, as staying.
Staying (yathāvasthita) is the method that is no method — anupāya named by performance, not by label.
anu-p01.inference: No method is enjoined; staying is the method that is no method. Anupāya named by performance.
uncertainties: Whether 'suniścita' (well-decided) is an adjective of truth or a separate noun is unresolved.
Whether 'japābhyāsaprayāso na ca' is one token or several is unresolved (kept as printed).

anu-p02.speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person)
anu-p02.question: Is saṃsāra real, and what follows?
premises: Saṃsāra is not, in truth (tattvatas), for body-holders (tanubhṛtām).
Of bondage, what news (vārtā)? If bondage never truly is anyone's (bandho yasya na jātu), the liberation-rite (muktikriyā) is false (vitathā) for the free.
Diagnosis: an error-maker (mithyāmohakṛt), a heap of four delusions — rope, snake, shadow, ghost.
Rule: abandon nothing (mā kiṃcit tyaja), grasp nothing (mā gṛhāṇa); live (vihara) healthy (svasthaḥ), staying (yathāvasthitaḥ).
anu-p02.inference: Saṃsāra is delusion; bondage is unreal; the liberation-rite is false; abandon nothing, grasp nothing, stay.
uncertainties: Whether 'muktasya muktikriyā' means 'liberation-rite for the free' or 'rite of the liberated' is unresolved.
Whether 'vihara' is imperative or indicative is unresolved.

anu-p03.speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person)
anu-p03.question: What difference in the unsurpassed?
premises: Worship, worshipper, worshipped — what difference-course in the unsurpassed?
Transition: of whom, by whom effected, who enters? In the oneness of anuttara, what talk, what differentiated path?
Māyā, not different from consciousness-nonduality, in otherness, though different — alas, stands.
All is pure own-experience-nature; vain thought, do not.
anu-p03.inference: Worship-difference is Māyā: it stands as other without being different from consciousness-nonduality. All is pure own-experience-nature.
uncertainties: Whether 'māyeyam' is 'this Māyā' or 'Māyā, this [illusion]' is unresolved.
Whether 'bhinnā api' (though different) modifies Māyā or the illusion is unresolved.

anu-p04.speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person)
anu-p04.question: What is bliss, and how is it found?
premises: Bliss (ānandaḥ) here (atra) is not (na) wealth-middle-intoxication (vittamadhyamadavana).
Nor (naiva) like enjoying women (aṅganāsaṅgavat); nor lamp-sun-moon-made (dīpārkendukṛta) splendour-multitude (prabhāprakaravat); nor (naiva) even the light-rise (prakāśodayaḥ) as commonly pictured.

Joy (harṣaḥ) with gathered-difference-liberation-bliss-ground (saṃbhṛtabhedamuktisukhabhūr), like burden-lowering (bhārāvatāropamaḥ), is the attainment (prāptiḥ) of the forgotten treasure (vismṛtanidheḥ) of the all-nonduality state (sarvādvaitapadasya): the light-rise (prakāśodayaḥ).
Bliss = prakāśodaya: difference gathered, burden set down, treasure remembered.
anu-p04.inference: Bliss is neither pleasure nor splendour but joy like burden-lowering — the attainment of the forgotten treasure.
uncertainties: Whether 'saṃbhṛtabhedamuktisukhabhūr' is one compound or several is unresolved.
Whether 'prakāśodaya' in the first half and second half refers to the same or different light-rise is unresolved.

anu-p05.speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person address)
anu-p05.question: Why not delight in variety?
premises: Passion, aversion, pleasure, displeasure, rise, dissolution, I-ness, misery and the rest — things shining-forth, universe-bodied — are not different-natured.
Whosever manifestation you suddenly see — having regarded (avekṣya) that-that (tattattad) one-self-natured (ekātmatā) consciousness-form (saṃvidrūpam) —
Why (kiṃ na) do you delight (ramase), full (nirbharaḥ) of that contemplation (tadbhāvanā)?
Regard is the whole practice: see variety as one-self-natured consciousness-form — delight is the only consistent response.
anu-p05.inference: Variety is one nature; regard it as consciousness-form, and delight is the only consistent response.
uncertainties: Whether 'ekātmatāsaṃvidrūpa' is one compound or several is unresolved.
Whether 'ramase' is indicative or imperative is unresolved.

anu-p06.speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person)
anu-p06.question: Whence the truth of things?
premises: Former non-being (pūrvābhāva), being (bhava), action (kriyā) — indeed (hi) suddenly (sahasā) things (bhāvāḥ) always (sadā) in this existence (asmin bhave) — of middle-formed (madhyākāra) transformation (vikāra), confusion (saṃkaravatāṃ) of them (teṣām): whence (kutaḥ) truth (satyatā)?
In non-truth (niḥsatye), unsteady (capale), manifold (prapañcanicaye), dream-delusion (svapnabhrame), clever (peśale) —
From doubt-fear-stain-reasoning-contriving transcended (śaṅkātaṅkakalaṅkayuktikalanātītaḥ): awakened (prabuddhaḥ), become (bhava).
Four obstacles — doubt, fear, stain, reasoning — with reasoning listed last among the fetters.
anu-p06.inference: Things lack truth; the only response is awakening: transcend doubt, fear, stain, reasoning; awaken.
uncertainties: Whether 'madhyākāra' means middle-formed or of middle-form is unresolved.
Whether 'peśala' means clever or cunning is unresolved.
Whether 'bhava' (become) is imperative or indicative is unresolved.

anu-p07.speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person)
anu-p07.question: Do things arise, and whence the universe-glory?
premises: Of things (bhāvānām) no arising (na samudbhavaḥ) is — natural (sahajaḥ), by your contemplation (tvadbhāvitā) they shine (bhānti).
Non-true (niḥsatyāḥ) too (api), truth (satyatām) they partake (bhajanti) by experience-delusion (anubhavabhrāntyā) for a moment (kṣaṇam).
This universe-glory (eṣa viśvamahimā) will-born from you (tvatsaṅkalpajaḥ); its birth (janma) from elsewhere (anyataḥ) is not (nāsti).
Hence (tasmāt) you shine (bhāsi) by splendor (vibhavena) in worlds (bhuvaneṣu) — one (ekaḥ), though (api), many-selfed (anekātmakaḥ).
anu-p07.inference: No arising; things shine by contemplation; non-true borrows momentary truth; universe-glory is will-born; you shine one-yet-many.
uncertainties: Whether 'anubhavabhrānti' means experience's delusion or delusion of experience is unresolved.
Whether 'ekopy anekātmakaḥ' means 'one, though many-selfed' or 'one, yet (becoming) many-selfed' is unresolved.

anu-p08.speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person)
anu-p08.question: What shines in the mirror, and what follows from knowing it?
premises: What true, what untrue, little-much, eternal, not eternal, what Māyā-stained, what self-pure — shines (rājate) in the consciousness-mirror (ciddarpaṇe).
All opposites, one mirror; the mirror doesn't sort them.
That all (tat sarvaṃ), from own-grasping-consciousness-rise (svavimarśasaṃvidudayāt), form-light-natured (rūpaprakāśātmakam), having known (jñātvā) —
— own-experience-risen (svānubhavādhirūḍha) glory (mahimā): Lordhood (viśveśvaratvam) — worship (bhaja).
anu-p08.inference: All opposites shine in the consciousness-mirror; knowing that all is own-grasping-consciousness-rise = glory = Lordhood; worship.
uncertainties: Whether 'svavimarśasaṃvidudaya' is one compound or several is unresolved.
Whether 'rūpaprakāśātmaka' modifies 'tat sarvam' or 'mahimā' is unresolved.
Whether 'bhaja' is imperative or indicative is unresolved.

anu-p01.plain_english: Transition here is no method at all — not contemplation, not speech-connection, not discussion, not visualization, not steadying, not japa-practice-effort. So what is well-decided? Speak the supreme truth, and hear it: not renouncer, not possessor — enjoy happiness, wholly, as staying.
anu-p01.sanskrit_cite: saṃkrāmaḥ atra na bhāvanā na ca kathāyuktiḥ na carcā na ca dhyānaṃ vā na ca dhāraṇā na ca japābhyāsaprayāso na ca tat kiṃ | nāma suniścitaṃ vada paraṃ satyaṃ ca tac śrūyatām na tyāgī na parigrahī bhaja sukhaṃ sarvam yathāvasthitaḥ

anu-p02.plain_english: Saṃsāra is not, in truth, for body-holders — of bondage, what news? Bondage never truly is for anyone — so for the free, liberation-rite is false. This error-maker is rope-snake-shadow-ghost-delusion. Abandon nothing; grasp nothing; live healthy, staying as you are.
anu-p02.sanskrit_cite: saṃsāraḥ asti na tattvatas tanubhṛtām bandhasya vārtā eva kā bandhaḥ yasya na jātu tasya vitathā | muktasya muktikriyā eṣaḥ mithyāmohakṛt rajjubhujagacchāyāpiśācabhramaḥ mā kiṃcit tyaja mā gṛhāṇa vihara svasthaḥ yathāvasthitaḥ

anu-p03.plain_english: Worship, worshipper, worshipped — what a difference-course in the unsurpassed? Transition — of whom, by whom effected, and who is the entry-course? This Māyā, not different from consciousness-nonduality, in otherness, though different — alas, stands. All is pure own-experience-nature. Thought in vain — do not do.
anu-p03.sanskrit_cite: pūjapūjakapūjya bhedasaraṇiḥ keyam kathā anuttare saṃkrāmaḥ kila kasya kena vidadhe ko vā praveśakramaḥ māyeyam | na cidadvayāt paratayā bhinnā api aho vartate sarvam svānubhavasvabhāvavimalaṃ cintāṃ vṛthā mā kṛthāḥ

anu-p04.plain_english: Bliss here is not wealth-middle-intoxication, nor like enjoying women, nor lamp-sun-moon-made splendour-multitude — nor is it the light-rise. Joy with gathered-difference-liberation-bliss-ground, like burden-lowering, is the attainment of the forgotten treasure of the all-nonduality state — the light-rise.
anu-p04.sanskrit_cite: ānandaḥ atra na vittamadhya madavan naivāṅganāsaṅgavat dīpārkendukṛta prabhāprakaravan naiva | prakāśodayaḥ harṣaḥ saṃbhṛtabhedamuktisukhabhūr bhārāvatāropamaḥ sarvādvaitapadasya vismṛtanidheḥ prāptiḥ prakāśodayaḥ

anu-p05.plain_english: Passion, aversion, pleasure, displeasure, rise and fall, I-ness, misery and the rest — things shining forth, universe-bodied, are not different-natured. Whosever manifestation you suddenly see — having regarded it as one-self-natured consciousness-form — why do you not delight, full of contemplation?
anu-p05.sanskrit_cite: rāga dveṣa sukha asukha udaya laya ahaṃkāra dainya ādayo ye bhāvāḥ pravibhānti viśvavapuṣo bhinnasvabhāvā | na te vyaktiṃ paśyasi yasya yasya sahasā tattattat ekātmatā saṃvidrūpam avekṣya kiṃ na ramase tad bhāvanānirbharaḥ

anu-p06.plain_english: Former non-being, being, action — things always, suddenly, in this existence: middle-formed, transformation-confused — whence their truth? In the non-true, unsteady, manifold, clever dream-delusion — transcending doubt, fear, stain, and reasoning's contriving: awakened, become.
anu-p06.sanskrit_cite: pūrva abhāva bhava kriyā hi sahasā bhāvāḥ sadā 'smin bhave madhyākāra vikāra | saṃkaravatām teṣām kutaḥ satyatā niḥsatye capale prapañcanicaye svapnabhrame peśale śaṅkātaṅkakalaṅkayuktikalanātītaḥ prabuddho bhava

anu-p07.plain_english: Of things there is no arising; naturally, by your contemplation they shine; even the non-true partakes of truth for a moment, through experience's delusion. This universe-glory is will-born from you, birth from elsewhere it has none; hence by splendor you shine in worlds — one, yet many-selfed.
anu-p07.sanskrit_cite: bhāvānāṃ na samudbhavo 'sti sahajas tvadbhāvitā bhānty amī niḥsatyā api satyatām anubhavabhrāntyā bhajanti kṣaṇam eṣa viśvamahimā | tvatsaṅkalpajaḥ nāsty asya janmā anyataḥ tasmāt tvaṃ vibhavena bhāsi bhuvaneṣv ekopy anekātmakaḥ

anu-p08.plain_english: What true, what untrue, little-much, eternal, not eternal, what Māyā-stained, what self-pure — in the consciousness-mirror shines. That all, from own-grasping-consciousness-rise, form-light-natured, having known — own-experience-risen glory: Lordhood — worship.
anu-p08.sanskrit_cite: yat satyaṃ yad asatyam alpabahulaṃ nityaṃ na nityaṃ ca yat māyāmalinaṃ yad ātmavimalaṃ | ciddarpaṇe rājate tat sarvaṃ svavimarśasaṃvidudayād rūpaprakāśātmakaṃ jñātvā svānubhavādhirūḍha mahimā viśveśvaratvaṃ bhaja

essence: No method is enjoined: contemplation, speech-connection, discussion, visualization, steadying, japa-practice-effort — all denied. The question replaces the hunt for method: what stands well-decided? Speak it, hear it. The answer is two refusals and one command: not renouncer, not possessor — enjoy happiness, wholly, as staying. Staying (yathāvasthita) is the method that is no method — anupāya named by performance, not by label.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of recognition (pratyabhijñā); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at method cleared and staying named. The rasa is the tranquility of anupāya — no effort, no progress, no practice, just staying. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as śānta: the relish of the unsurpassed.

essence: Saṃsāra is unreal for the embodied; bondage never truly is for anyone, so the liberation-rite is false. The error is a fourfold delusion-heap — rope, snake, shadow, ghost. Abandon nothing, grasp nothing; live healthy, staying.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of recognition (pratyabhijñā); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at bondage denied and the two prohibitions. The rasa is the tranquility of anupāya — no liberation-rite needed, just staying.

essence: Worship, worshipper, worshipped — what difference-course in the unsurpassed? Transition: of whom, by whom effected, who enters? Māyā, not different from consciousness-nonduality, stands as other — alas. All is pure own-experience-nature; vain thought, do not.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of recognition (pratyabhijñā); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at Māyā standing as other without being different. The rasa is the tranquility of non-duality — no worship-difference in the unsurpassed.

essence: Bliss is neither wealth-intoxication nor lamp-sun-moon splendour. Joy with gathered-difference-liberation-bliss-ground, like burden-lowering, is the attainment of the forgotten treasure of the all-nonduality state — the light-rise. Bliss = prakāśodaya: difference gathered, burden set down, treasure remembered.

rasa.sthayibhava: ānanda (bliss) as the forgotten treasure found
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of finding (prāpti); the vyabhicāri is joy (harṣa) of burden-lowering. The rasa is bliss as ingress into fullness, not as pleasure or splendour — the forgotten treasure remembered.

essence: Passions through misery — the whole catalogue of feeling-states, universe-bodied — are not different-natured. Whatever manifestation you suddenly see, regard as one-self-natured consciousness-form: why not delight, contemplation-full? Variety is one nature; the only consistent response to seeing it as consciousness-form is delight.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of delight (rati); the vyabhicāri is joy (harṣa) of seeing variety as one-self-natured consciousness. The rasa is bliss as delight, not as possession — seeing variety as consciousness-form, delight is the only consistent response.

essence: Former non-being, being, action — things always, suddenly here, middle-formed and confused: whence their truth? In the non-true, unsteady, manifold, clever dream-delusion — transcend doubt, fear, stain, reasoning's contriving: awakened, become. Things lack truth; the only response is awakening.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of awakening (prabodha); the vyabhicāri is clarity (prasāda) of transcending the four fetters. The rasa is the tranquility of awakening — not the thrill of argument but the peace of seeing things as non-true and waking up.

essence: Of things no arising; naturally they shine by your contemplation, even the non-true borrowing momentary truth. This universe-glory is will-born from you, birth from elsewhere denied; hence you shine in worlds — one, yet many-selfed. Nonduality without cancelling multiplicity: one, yet many-selfed.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of recognition (pratyabhijñā); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at one, yet many-selfed. The rasa is the tranquility of non-dual self-manifestation — the Absolute shining in worlds without being divided.

essence: All opposites shine in the consciousness-mirror: true/untrue, little/much, eternal/non-eternal, Māyā-stained/self-pure. That all, from own-grasping-consciousness-rise, form-light-natured, having known — own-experience-risen glory: Lordhood — worship. Knowing that all opposites shine in the mirror from one's own grasping consciousness = glory = Lordhood; its last word is the imperative it opened with the stance for.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of Lordhood (viśveśvaratva); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at all opposites shining in the mirror from one's own grasping consciousness. The rasa is the tranquility of Lordhood — the hymn that began in anupāya ends in worship.

lines: No crossing here by method — no contemplation, no reasoned talk, no inquiry, no visualization, no fixing, no straining at mantra-practice.
So what stands well decided? Speak the highest truth — and hear it: neither renouncer nor possessor — enjoy happiness, all of it, abiding as you are.
anu-p01.sanskrit_cite: saṃkrāmo 'tra na bhāvanā na ca kathāyuktir na carcā na ca dhyānaṃ vā na ca dhāraṇā na ca japābhyāsaprayāso na ca | tat kiṃ nāma suniścitaṃ vada paraṃ satyaṃ ca tac chrūyatām: na tyāgī na parigrahī — bhaja sukhaṃ sarvam yathāvasthitaḥ

lines: For body-bearers, Saṃsāra in truth is not — of bondage, what news?
Bondage never truly is anyone’s — so the liberation-rite is false.
This error-maker: rope-snake-shadow-ghost delusion. Abandon nothing; grasp nothing —
live healthy, staying as you are.
anu-p02.sanskrit_cite: saṃsāraḥ asti na tattvatas tanubhṛtām bandhasya vārtā eva kā bandhaḥ yasya na jātu tasya vitathā | muktasya muktikriyā eṣaḥ mithyāmohakṛt rajjubhujagacchāyāpiśācabhramaḥ mā kiṃcit tyaja mā gṛhāṇa vihara svasthaḥ yathāvasthitaḥ

Transition indeed — of whom, by whom made, who walks the entry-course?
This Māyā — no different from consciousness-nonduality — stands as other, though different. Alas.
Everything is pure own-experience-nature. Vain thought — do not.

lines: Bliss here is not wealth-middle-intoxication, nor like enjoying women,
nor lamp-sun-moon-made splendour-multitudes — nor even the light-rise.
Joy — difference gathered, freed in bliss-ground, like the lowering of a burden —
is the forgotten treasure found of the all-nonduality state: the light-rise.
anu-p04.sanskrit_cite: ānandaḥ atra na vittamadhya madavan naivāṅganāsaṅgavat dīpārkendukṛta prabhāprakaravan naiva | prakāśodayaḥ harṣaḥ saṃbhṛtabhedamuktisukhabhūr bhārāvatāropamaḥ sarvādvaitapadasya vismṛtanidheḥ prāptiḥ prakāśodayaḥ

lines: Passion, aversion, pleasure, pain, rise and fall, I-sense, misery and the rest — these states, shining forth, bodied of the universe, are of no separate nature.
Whatever form you suddenly see — see it as consciousness of one self-nature: why not delight, full of contemplating it?
anu-p05.sanskrit_cite: rāgadveṣasukhāsukhodayalayāhaṅkāradainyādayo ye bhāvāḥ pravibhānti viśvavapuṣo bhinnasvabhāvā na te | vyaktiṃ paśyasi yasya yasya sahasā tattattadekātmatāsaṃvidrūpam avekṣya kiṃ na ramase tadbhāvanānirbharaḥ

lines: Past non-being, being, doing — things, always, suddenly, in this becoming, half-formed and mixed in change: what truth could they have?
In the untrue, restless, teeming, clever dream-delusion — past doubting, fearing, staining, and reason’s scheming: awake — become.
anu-p06.sanskrit_cite: pūrvābhāvabhavakriyā hi sahasā bhāvāḥ sadā 'smin bhave madhyākāravikārasaṃkaravatāṃ teṣāṃ kutaḥ satyatā | niḥsatye capale prapañcanicaye svapnabhrame peśale śaṅkātaṅkakalaṅkayuktikalanātītaḥ prabuddho bhava

lines: Things do not arise; by nature they shine through your beholding — even the untrue partakes of truth for a moment, through experience’s delusion.
This glory of worlds is will-born of You, with birth from nowhere else — so in splendor You shine through the worlds, one and yet many-selfed.
anu-p07.sanskrit_cite: bhāvānāṃ na samudbhavo 'sti sahajas tvadbhāvitā bhānty amī niḥsatyā api satyatām anubhavabhrāntyā bhajanti kṣaṇam | tvatsaṅkalpaja eṣa viśvamahimā nāsty asya janmānyataḥ tasmāt tvaṃ vibhavena bhāsi bhuvaneṣv ekopy anekātmakaḥ

lines: What is true, what untrue, little or much, lasting or lasting-not, Māyā-stained or self-pure — all shines in the mirror of consciousness.
All that — risen from self-grasping consciousness, natured as form and light — know it: glory mounted on your own experience — worship lordship of all.
anu-p08.sanskrit_cite: yat satyaṃ yad asatyam alpabahulaṃ nityaṃ na nityaṃ ca yat yan māyāmalinaṃ yad ātmavimalaṃ ciddarpaṇe rājate | tat sarvaṃ svavimarśasaṃvidudayād rūpaprakāśātmakaṃ jñātvā svānubhavādhirūḍhamahimā viśveśvaratvaṃ bhaja

notes.craft_notes: Sthāyin: ānanda as forgotten-treasure-found; bhakti as prāpti (finding); vyabhicāri harṣa of burden-lowering. Sanskrit-first: na…na…na (triple refusal — wealth/women/splendour, then pictured-light refused too); bhāraharaṇam iva (LIKE burden-lowering — iva simile kept as simile); smṛti (FOUND-treasure — the forgotten remembered). Rows: 9 (refusal catalogue — each pleasure named then refused; naming IS the finding), 10 (burden image left standing, no gloss), 1 (light-rise AFFIRMED last — the refused word returns; ring closes whether same-or-different, held open). Close: ‘the light-rise’. Rupture: ‘Joy —’ (refusals turn to naming — the dash after Joy holds the turn). Rejected: gilding — killed: bluntness is the music; ‘treasure-trove’ — killed: domesticates the finding; deciding same-vs-different light — killed: held open (the ring's ambiguity IS the verse). Read aloud: BLISS-here is NOT wealth-MIDD-le … NOR lamp-SUN-moon-MADE … JOY — DIFF-er-ence GA-thered, FREED in BLISS-ground, LIKE the LOW-er-ing OF a BUR-den — IS the for-GOTT-en TREA-sure FOUND.

reads_against.argmap: What is bliss, and how is it found? → Bliss is neither pleasure nor splendour but joy like burden-lowering — the attainment of the forgotten treasure.
c1_essence: Bliss is neither wealth-intoxication nor lamp-sun-moon splendour. Joy with gathered-difference-liberation-bliss-ground, like burden-lowering, is the attainment of the forgotten treasure of the all-nonduality state — the light-rise. Bliss = prakāśodaya: difference gathered, burden set down, treasure remembered.
